outcome: All same-tab departures await checkpoints then use the shared unsaved-progress guard. Cancel preserves recovery/export; explicit discard navigates. Removed saves are distinct from pending progress, reviews drain queued/observer-created checkpoints, removal stays paused, and already-flushed disposal avoids new Web Locks so native Chromium BFCache survives. All dungeon checkpoints share #365 locking.
ablation: Reuses existing mutation queues, dialog owner, departure confirmation, records store and typed storage primitives. One explicit removal flag distinguishes deleted bytes from pending progress; review barriers solve demonstrated asynchronous handoff failures. No dependency, new storage journal, service or broad redesign.
limits: Native focus/BFCache assertions are Chromium-specific; WebKit retains synthetic visibility/focus plus real navigation/resume.
Abrupt termination may lose the last bounded playtime checkpoint interval.
Old clients may reject upgraded saves/history. Preserve raw bytes and recover with a statistics-capable build; reverse old-client readability is not claimed.
Focused PR qualification, not a clean full-regression claim.
git: One reviewed commit per PR, stacked 365 -> 368 -> 369 on main. Retain high/high/medium risk labels. No release tags or merges. If later squash-merging a parent, carry the dependent branch onto its resulting main commit before merging it.
